rows.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI will create ‘hundreds of thousands’ of new jobs—including for people who want to ‘make things with their hands’
rows.standfirst: Unlike Bill Gates, the billionaire Nvidia CEO is bullish that AI will create more jobs than it eliminates—and skilled trade professionals stand to benefit.

rows.title: As Gen Z flocks back to accounting, EY is investing $100 million in bonuses for employees who prove they have human skills
rows.standfirst: EY is betting on human skills like judgment and adaptability, offering workers cash awards of up to $25,000 as AI transforms accounting.

rows.title: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus once told Gen Z to ‘never assume’ they know as much as others—he says it’s the mindset hack that will push you forward
rows.standfirst: Apple CEO John Ternus shared the mindset hack that steered his 25-year career at the $4.6 trillion tech giant: “Assume you’re as smart as anyone else.”

rows.title: Mark Cuban bought a $25 million mansion sight unseen—and got it for 50% off. His secret? ‘The best guaranteed return on investment’
rows.standfirst: Cuban dropped millions on a mansion he’d never set foot in, but has zero regrets. The deal captures how billionaires think differently about money.

rows.title: Gen Z can’t figure out how to talk to their millennial and Gen X bosses—and it’s becoming a workplace crisis
rows.standfirst: From email etiquette to office jargon, the unwritten rules of workplace communication are getting harder to read across generations.

rows.title: Chicago Fed’s Austan Goolsbee wants to get back to ‘old-school’ economics: Focused on ordinary Americans, mindful of AI hype, and sharp on inflation
rows.standfirst: Exclusive: “If there were going to be something that shook the consumers, it would shake the economy,” president Goolsbee tells Fortune.

rows.title: One of the fastest-growing jobs in Silicon Valley sends engineers straight to customers’ offices to get AI up and running—and pays more than $188,000
rows.standfirst: Silicon Valley tech giants are copying Palantir’s playbook by hiring engineers to work directly with customers—and paying them nearly $200K to do so.

rows.title: He failed the military pilot eye test—so he built a $1 million-a-day traffic company and bought flying lessons. Now he’s Top Gun’s stunt pilot
rows.standfirst: Top Gun’s stunt pilot built a traffic company as a teen. Now he’s making millions—enough to fund flying lessons and a $2 million helicopter.

rows.title: ‘I don’t think there’s a floor’: Workers’ share of America’s income is at a record low before the AI boom even begins
rows.standfirst: EY-Parthenon chief economist Gregory Daco says that the economy’s surprising productivity gains so far predate AI.

rows.title: Who runs the labor market? Women accounted for 98% of U.S. job gains in August
rows.standfirst: The economy added 162,000 jobs, nearly triple forecasts, but the gains were unusually concentrated among women.

rows.title: DOJ expands beef price probe to eight retailers, including Walmart and Amazon, with inflation a key issue ahead of midterm elections
rows.standfirst: The new probe into retailers seems to build on the department’s antitrust investigation into meatpackers.

rows.title: Job seekers are waiting for the ‘September Surge.’ Economists say there’s something behind the hype and explain why it’s a good time to apply
rows.standfirst: There are real seasonal patterns behind the September hiring hype, but more job postings don’t necessarily mean faster hiring.

rows.title: Trump says ‘stupidity causes inflation’ and threatens to stop trade with foreign countries in retaliation for higher interest rates
rows.standfirst: Trump declared it “crazy” that the stock markets fell Friday on inflation concerns.

rows.title: These industries will lead hiring in the next decade, with just one sector accounting for more than a third of all new jobs
rows.standfirst: The healthcare and social assistance industry, which will expand employment by 2.2 million over the next decade.

rows.title: After 30 years in aerospace, these brothers retired from corporate life and work at Disney: ‘I’m finished being married to my laptop and phone’
rows.standfirst: Jerry and Peter Wong grew up going to Disney every year. Now in their 60’s, they work as a photographer and ride worker at the California theme parks.

rows.title: Upcoming inflation data could determine if the Federal Reserve hikes interest rates soon, leaving Wall Street on edge
rows.standfirst: The producer price index comes out on Thursday, and the consumer price index comes out on Friday.

rows.title: Even Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is worried about Iran’s economy and ‘social cohesion’ as U.S. pressure gets tougher to withstand
rows.standfirst: “There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services.”

rows.title: As Wall Street shifts expectations towards a Fed rate hike, the White House turns up the pressure on Warsh’s central bank
rows.standfirst: “High interest rates put the U.S.A. at a very unfair disadvantage, and I won’t allow that to happen!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

rows.title: ‘The math does not lie’: Why Austin only built 543 low-income homes while delivering 15,000 for the middle class
rows.standfirst: Austin officials set a goal of building 20,000 units between 2018 and 2027 for extremely low-income people — 17% of the city’s households.

rows.title: Cutting the cord was supposed to save money. Eight streaming services now cost a combined $139 a month
rows.standfirst: Choosing ads wherever possible still costs nearly $90 a month, leaving households to chase bundles, cancel subscriptions and rotate services.

rows.title: Inflation won’t die. Now the bond market is daring the Fed to do something about it
rows.standfirst: The 10-year Treasury yield is nearing 5% as oil, tariffs and sticky service prices raise fears that Kevin Warsh may have to restart the rate-hiking cycle.

rows.title: Scott Bessent dared the $32 trillion bond market with ‘I am the house now’ statement. It didn’t listen
rows.standfirst: After helping lift the yen, Bessent is finding the much larger Treasury market harder to tame as yields push toward 5%.

rows.title: Exec gave his Gen Z kids a list of ‘daddy tips’ when they became old enough to work—it included showing up on time and ‘bringing value to a meeting’
rows.standfirst: Bosses say Gen Z lack basic people skills. One exec turned decades of career advice into a cheat sheet for his own daughters before they started work

rows.title: Even low-ranked colleges can be a ticket to six figures: Graduates earn $100K+ a decade later—more than twice as much as high school grads
rows.standfirst: Nearly every school in a new ranking has median earnings above $90,000, showing students don’t necessarily need to attend Harvard to make a strong salary.

rows.title: Women hold more U.S. jobs than men—but still earn far less starting the day they graduate
rows.standfirst: Female workers are driving nearly all of America’s job growth as men keep leaving the labor force. Their paychecks tell the opposite story—and the gap only widens with age.

rows.title: Wall Street thought the Powell hike was over. Now Kevin Warsh has his ‘back against the wall’
rows.standfirst: Hotter inflation, above $100 oil and a 10-year Treasury yield flirting with 5% have put another round of rate hikes back on the table.

rows.title: Housing market: Mortgage rates rise for third straight week to highest level since June 2025 while home sales fall for third month in a row
rows.standfirst: The benchmark 30-year fixed rate mortgage rose to 6.76% from 6.71% last week. One year ago, the average rate was 6.35%.

rows.title: Trump’s childhood home sells for $1.9 million after prior owner bought it for $835,000 last year, when it was a mold-ridden den of feral cats
rows.standfirst: Tommy Lin, had purchased the five-bedroom, three-bathroom home last year for $835,000 after it sat vacant and neglected for years.

rows.title: Mortgage lending standards are so tight that homebuyers must have ‘pristine’ credit histories, study says, as sales head for 31-year low
rows.standfirst: “These changes helped to reduce delinquencies and defaults but also made it more difficult for many Americans to qualify for a mortgage.”

rows.title: The new American retirement fear: working until you die
rows.standfirst: In a strained economy, more Americans suspect their worst retirement fear is coming true—that they won’t get to retire at all.

rows.title: Anne Hathaway says she was spammed with ChatGPT-written thank you notes after hiring for a recent role: ‘Nobody on that list gets that job’
rows.standfirst: Anne Hathaway received the same AI-written thank you note from every candidate—and Meryl Streep said what every boss is thinking: “That’s just tragic.”

rows.title: Billionaire Mike Bloomberg was fired after dedicating 15 years of his career to Salomon Brothers—the next morning, he founded his media empire
rows.standfirst: Mike Bloomberg started at Salomon Brothers as a clerk making $9,000 a year, making his way up to partner, before getting the boot. He has no hard feelings, and learned critical lessons from the rejection.

rows.title: Even Americans earning more than $155,000 now call themselves ‘working class’—a sign of how far the affordability crisis has spread
rows.standfirst: A new Pew study found 60% of U.S. adults identify as working class, up from 54% two years ago—and half of the country’s top earners say the label fits.

rows.title: Good pay, high demand, no takers. The status problem behind America’s trades shortage.
rows.standfirst: Retirements, outdated perceptions, and a lack of career awareness are making it harder to fill in-demand jobs in the skilled trades.

rows.title: Uber’s CEO hints at cheaper rides after the company announced 3,300 corporate jobs
rows.standfirst: Dara Khosrowshahi said AI has partly created a “tailwind” for the company on productivity.

rows.title: Trump tells Americans not to ‘kill the golden goose’ rejecting voters’ turn against AI and data centers
rows.standfirst: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon are uniting against AI just as Trump, the other main character from the 2016 era in politics, stands for acceleration.

rows.title: As 10-year Treasury yield hits 5%, debt hawks are eyeing a national debt spiral: ‘If this isn’t a wake-up call, I don’t know what will be’
rows.standfirst: “A fiscal crisis, once unthinkable, is now a distinct possibility.”

rows.title: Shrinkflation is coming for pro sports: The cost of watching the NFL jumped 28.6%—and attending a game 72%—since 2015
rows.standfirst: To watch all the football action this season, you will need to open your wallet more—for less.

rows.title: Millennials are winning the AI talent wars—they’re getting 60% of all the top AI jobs and earning $236K salaries. But most of them are men.
rows.standfirst: The highest-paid AI managers have two things in common: a degree, and being a man. While women and workers without one are stuck in AI’s lowest-paying jobs.

rows.title: Hot or not? The economy’s fate rests on Kevin Warsh’s answer to one key question
rows.standfirst: Oil near $110, 5% Treasury yields, an AI investment boom and stubborn inflation have revived a question the Fed hasn’t faced in years: Is America overheating?

rows.title: 1 in 3 Gen Z and millennials are stuck in their parents’ home—now, Airbnb is swooping in with a $250 million fund for affordable rental homes
rows.standfirst: A record 25.2 million U.S. adults under the age of 35 lived with their parents last year. Airbnb is hoping to be “part of the solution” for affordable housing.

rows.title: The Fed unanimously agrees to hike interest rates for the first time since 2023, despite Trump’s call for the ‘lowest rates’ in the world
rows.standfirst: Inflation has been above 2% for five years. The Fed just decided that was long enough.

rows.title: America’s bedrot era: How the dopamine recession created the ‘couch economy’
rows.standfirst: New spending data shows how much of the economy now depends on people staying home, and a chase for quick, easy hits of stimulation may be driving it.

rows.title: GM CEO Mary Barra says America has a ‘societal problem’ with skilled trades—and is putting $200 million behind training Gen Z to work with their hands
rows.standfirst: General Motors invested $200 million in skilled trades last year. Its CEO Mary Barra says they could offer Gen Z a more “AI-proof” path to six-figure pay.

rows.title: Ryan Serhant says the American city isn’t dying—wealth is ‘multiplying,’ and buyers are flocking to Ohio, Alabama, and the Carolinas
rows.standfirst: The Owning Manhattan star says the wealthy are diversifying into cheaper, less obvious markets.

rows.title: ‘It’s a raise against Trump:’ Despite inflation being ahead of target for five years, Trump says the Fed’s latest hike is political
rows.standfirst: “The problem they have is that we have the greatest economy in history … so they’re raising that only for political reasons, and that’s a raise against Trump.”

rows.title: College grads shut out of AI-exposed majors since 2022 are ending up in retail and food service instead of the white-collar jobs they studied for
rows.standfirst: Entry-level hiring dried up after ChatGPT, and graduates who majored in those fields are settling for lower-paying service work instead.

rows.title: Oil is back above $100—but economists say that number isn’t the real threat to the U.S. economy
rows.standfirst: Gas takes up less household income than it once did, but record diesel prices and refinery shortages could still curb spending.

rows.title: ‘Stealth wealth’ is reshaping luxury real estate: How the ultrarich buy multimillion-dollar mansions off the books
rows.standfirst: The ultrawealthy now treat visibility as a liability and they’re paying to disappear from luxury real estate records.

rows.title: The bank account says no while the Europe group chat says YOLO. Gen Z is cutting spending—but not on little treats and last-minute trips
rows.standfirst: Even as everyday costs pile up, Gen Z is making room for what feels worth it.

rows.title: Hilton received 12,000 Gen Z applications for just 72 internship spots—its CHRO says AI has made the hospitality gigs more competitive
rows.standfirst: Only 0.4% of young applicants make it into Hilton’s early-career program—even more selective than Ivy League colleges.

rows.title: Zoom’s CEO agrees with Bill Gates, Jensen Huang, and Jamie Dimon: A 3-day workweek is coming soon thanks to AI
rows.standfirst: Zoom leader Eric Yuan admitted the technology will erase some human jobs—but those who keep their jobs will enjoy fewer working days.

rows.title: As high fuel costs force people to choose between filling up or buying groceries, Trump says ‘it’s a very inexpensive price to pay’ for the Iran war
rows.standfirst: “Gas prices matter because they’re one of the few economic indicators voters experience and see in real time,” said veteran Republican strategist Chris Wilson.

rows.title: The economy has undergone a structural transformation that ended the low-cost era. ‘The regime change in inflation and interest rates is the outcome’
rows.standfirst: The shift, in many ways, returns the economy to where it was before the financial crisis in December 2007 that lasted through June 2009.

rows.title: U.S. economy hits pivotal milestone: Spending on data centers and other information-processing hardware now exceeds housing investment
rows.standfirst: “We’re seeing a pivotal shift in the US economy: investment is shifting away from residential investment and towards computers.”

rows.title: Dollar General CEO says consumers making $100,000 a year don’t feel like high-income shoppers anymore as high gas prices and inflation reshape habits
rows.standfirst: “Having 2,000 items at or below $1 is very meaningful for the consumer, always has, but especially in this environment.”

rows.title: U.S. Treasury’s bond scheme is not a national debt management tool, say top economists, but it did show Wall Street what makes Scott Bessent flinch
rows.standfirst: “This can backfire because the market will look at this and say, ‘Well, the fact that you need to come out and say and do these things implies that this market has already lost the confidence of investors.'”

rows.title: Warren Buffett once called Berkshire Hathaway the ‘dumbest’ stock he ever bought—after 60 years, he’s stepped down with a $145 billion net worth
rows.standfirst: Billionaire Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman after 60 years at the $1 trillion business he once called “terrible” when buying.

rows.title: Indeed CEO says the job market is stuck in a ‘vicious cycle’ if 1,000 qualified candidates can’t get hired: ‘Something’s wrong’
rows.standfirst: Applicants are sending resumes into a black hole as hiring managers sift through AI-generated and fake applications. Indeed’s CEO says it’s a perfect storm

rows.title: $6 trillion a year in unpaid labor isn’t counted in GDP. Its absence from official stats distorts how we see growth, living standards and productivity
rows.standfirst: A new GAO report puts a price tag on unpaid household labor and shows why family income can look better on paper than it feels in real life

rows.title: ‘Skills nobody can take’: Meet a 20-year-old with a 4.5 GPA who skipped college for technical school to land an ‘AI-proof’ career
rows.standfirst: Alejandro Rodriguez was a gifted-and-talented student with a 4.5 GPA and every expectation of a four-year degree. He chose to become a Porsche technician instead

rows.title: Americans are turning to AI to survive a brutal housing market—37% would let it buy their next home with ‘minimal human involvement’
rows.standfirst: From estimating home values to comparing mortgage offers, buyers are leaning on AI to survive a market where rates are pushing back toward 7%.

rows.title: The 10-year Treasury yield just hit 5% for the first time since 2007 — is a 1970s-style ‘stagflation’ on the return?
rows.standfirst: From the pandemic to the war in Iran, the bond market has been on quite a ride to the 5% benchmark.

rows.title: Mortgage rates are nearing 7%, delivering another blow to a housing market already losing buyers and facing stalled sales
rows.standfirst: Home sales have fallen to their lowest pace in more than a year and sellers are offering concessions to lure back buyers

rows.title: DOGE’s push to shrink the federal workforce cost the Trump administration $6.7 billion for employees not to work
rows.standfirst: Elon Musk’s ‘Fork in the Road’ initiative was responsible for most of a 435% increase in administrative leave between 2023 and 2035, a Government Accountability Office report found.

rows.title: Gen Z’s iced coffee habit in interviews could be costing them jobs, recruiters warn: ‘It isn’t really about coffee’
rows.standfirst: Professionals and hiring experts are divided on the internet’s iced coffee debate—but the real issue could be changing workplace norms.

rows.title: D.C.’s affordability headache has a silver bullet, new study shows: Tackling $40 trillion national debt would boost household income by $36,000
rows.standfirst: “Deficit reduction can further reduce inflation by lowering self-reinforcing inflation expectations to the extent it reduces the likelihood that future policymakers will aim to inflate away the national debt.”

rows.title: Kevin Warsh might have to get a lot less popular on Capitol Hill as bond yields soar and rate expectations turn hawkish
rows.standfirst: “The direction of crude oil prices still bears on what happens to inflation globally and the decisions taken by central banks in response.”

rows.title: Cisco CEO warns workers who worry about change that ‘nothing’s going to feel good right now’ with AI
rows.standfirst: Chuck Robbins, the CEO of $415 billion tech company Cisco, urges leaders to not use AI as a “cost-reduction efficiency play” and cut staffers.

rows.title: U.S.-Iran conflict is causing unexpected problems for Americans: 65% of employees want jobs that help them avoid paying higher gas prices
rows.standfirst: 23% of employed Americans told a survey they were on the hunt for a role closer to home.

rows.title: Entry-level jobs were actually secret apprenticeships all along, and AI just cut the subsidy
rows.standfirst: Wharton professor Patrick Harker was president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia for a decade. He knows what a tight labor market looks like.

rows.title: Despite the entry-level job apocalypse, half of Gen Z are planning to look for new work elsewhere before the end of the year
rows.standfirst: A majority of Gen Zers are looking to switch jobs and take home a bigger paycheck, even as opportunities shrink and pay gains flatten.

rows.title: Social Security’s annual cost-of-living adjustment is coming soon. Here are the states where the biggest hike in years could have the most impact
rows.standfirst: The Senior Citizens League estimated the COLA for 2027 will be 3.5%, while the AARP projected a 3.6% hike.

rows.title: Libraries are becoming a cost-of-living hack, and some are seeing a surge in sign-ups
rows.standfirst: Libraries are drawing in users with free streaming, local business discounts, and tech help as the cost of living bites

rows.title: For Gen Z workers wary of college debt, Walmart offers a road to six figures without a degree
rows.standfirst: The retail giant is training store associates for in-demand roles as truck drivers, technicians, and opticians.

rows.title: The $40 trillion U.S. national debt is smaller than Japan’s relative to its economy—but economist warns America is still ‘the world’s largest debtor’
rows.standfirst: “Japan’s debt dynamics are fundamentally different from those of the United States … Japan is the world’s largest creditor nation. The U.S. is the world’s largest debtor.”

rows.title: An 87-year-old woman was evicted via stretcher from a Madrid apartment she lived in for decades, sparking mass protest against Spain’s housing crisis
rows.standfirst: The Bank of Spain estimated that the country had a shortage of about 550,000 homes last year, with Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia accounting for a substantial share.

rows.title: Gen Z aren’t ready for the workplace—and this youth job program CEO is giving them a crash course in emails and workplace etiquette to change that
rows.standfirst: Byron V. Garrett, the CEO of Genesys Works, says employers “want someone who’s ready to go to work,” so it’s training thousands of underserved U.S. teens.

rows.title: Baby boomers are setting up a showdown with millennials, aging in place and plunking down hundreds of thousands on renovating their homes
rows.standfirst: Millennials need homes, but because of high home prices and mortgage rates, baby boomers have little reason to sell.

rows.title: Thinking about buying stocks instead of a home as mortgage rates top 7%? The S&P 500 has blown away the housing market over the past decade
rows.standfirst: “Buying a home also bundles two very important, but very different, decisions: where to live, and how to invest a large chunk of your life savings.”

rows.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says he spends three hours a day on recruitment—and if his hiring managers don’t like his input, he tells them to leave
rows.standfirst: ‘I probably spend three hours a day recruiting,’ Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says. And he admits he stole the idea from his friend, ChatGPT boss Sam Altman.

rows.title: Trump’s hidden tax on every American: how diesel touches everything that hits your wallet
rows.standfirst: You probably don’t know how much more you’ve had to pay for stuff since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

rows.title: Billionaire David Rubenstein tells young workers to learn how to read and write in the AI era: ‘Learn how to speak effectively and persuasively’
rows.standfirst: The Carlyle cofounder says the core skills of reading and writing have made people “successful over the last several thousand years,” and will never change.

rows.title: AI may prove disinflationary because agents can negotiate contracts and deals to make your life cheaper, says top economist
rows.standfirst: Personalized AI agents “could ultimately be an important competitive, and disinflationary, force across the economy,” Jeremy Siegel wrote.

rows.title: ‘We are going to start looking a lot more like Europe’: Millennials are living at home into their 30s, signaling a major shift
rows.standfirst: A real estate expert tells Fortune that there’s a “secular shift” underway in American life: More young adults are “content” living at home with their parents.

rows.title: Funflation is fueling hobbies as Americans spend more on fun at home to avoid going out
rows.standfirst: The rising cost of airfare, eating out, and gas has made Americans pickier about their spending.

rows.title: Google data center lead says ‘hundreds of thousands’ of skilled trade jobs are open across the U.S.—and they’re ‘just waiting to be filled’
rows.standfirst: Despite growing backlash over data centers, trillions in AI investment are fueling a surge in high-paying skilled trades jobs across the U.S.

rows.title: Ford CEO Jim Farley teams with Jamie Dimon on $2 billion initiative as he fears the ‘backbone of the American Dream’ is crumbling
rows.standfirst: The State of America’s Skilled Trades report finds that employers will need to fill about 1.7 million skilled-trades openings each year through 2035.

rows.title: LinkedIn CEO says that job seekers are sending out 30% more applications than pre-pandemic—and it’s harder to ‘know who can actually do the job’
rows.standfirst: The job market has become an all-out AI arms race between applicants and recruiters.

rows.title: Carhartt CEO warns schools are steering Gen Z students away from a lucrative career path: Skilled trades can pay 32% more
rows.standfirst: Students interested in landing a six-figure trades job aren’t being set up for success, says Linda Hubbard—with half who start training never finish it.

rows.title: Mike Rowe on America’s great tradesperson shortage: ‘I don’t care what your politics are. Math doesn’t care, either’
rows.standfirst: At Ford Pro Accelerate, Rowe spoke alongside Education Secretary Linda McMahon and the Defense Department’s Mike Duffey about the divide between college and the trades.
